_schema: Registry of EVERY place a kept kernel falls back to torch (or a donor) instead of a custom/native path, with the reason and the roofline/limit justification. Maintained across the whole optimization + integration phase and SURFACED FOR REVIEW at phase end. A fallback is legitimate only if it is (a) strictly best-of (no regression at the fallback point) OR (b) at the measured limit for that case with no known lever left.
surface_at: end of optimization + integration phase (review gate)

fallbacks.custom_path: parallel std::nth_element O(S) set-select (used for M=1 and priority M=16/32/64)
fallbacks.reason: custom loses at M=8 (0.42x vs torch.topk): only 8 row-tasks spread over 64 threads underutilize the machine; torch.topk parallelizes the selection differently.
fallbacks.limit_justification: top-k is SELECTION, not GEMM -> no oneDNN/AMX primitive to exploit; op is tiny (sub-ms, minor forward slice). Explored: a 2-pass chunk->local-topk->merge kernel would close M=8 but adds code for a tiny op (diminishing returns). ACCEPTED AT THE LIMIT for now.
fallbacks.decided: option 1 — custom + torch.topk fallback at M=8 (wins priority, no regression anywhere)
fallbacks.revisit: if M=8 becomes hot after integration, or if a cheap finer-grain kernel is found
